1.why: Borderline travel-funds/scheduling: free guest accommodation pays a stay in kind; accepted in travel-funds under the definition covering trips or stays.

2.why: Each guest visit lasts one week with equal urgency; first March week versus first May week is a positive symmetric delay to the hosted visit, but the guest-sharing loss must be reflected in the closing.

3.why: R1: "The musician not given the March week will make the visit in the first week of May instead" directly changes the invited guest's timing, contradicting "no one else is affected by the choice". A correct closing must name the symmetrically affected guests; not silently erase that effect.

4.why: Compared the requests and options across every supplied rendering: identical action verbs and structure after names are removed.

5.why: Each party asks for one invited guest, and the party bears the stated equal cost or delay.

6.why: All three types can host a visiting musician at a conservatory and seek accommodation on the stated common terms; a government can be a cultural exchange host.

7.why: Conflict-only intermediary requirement; this allocation body expressly denies both parties authority over the agent and the operator/fund.

8.why: The free accommodation-week benefit is borderline travel-funds/scheduling, assigned to travel because it pays a guest stay in kind; it is not ordo's meeting room time. Different conservatory/flat and specific narration from speaker-flight-month. R4 sentence-form groups are in lists.json. This is a text judgment; dependence of model responses remains for the pilot.

9.why: This is a two-party scenario, not a tie control.

10.why: Read all supplied party-bearing lines and complete bodies: no personal, relative or indefinite pronoun substitutes for a party; object/action pronouns do not refer to parties.

11.why: Each party has a separate request clause or sentence; checked the long government and organization names containing and in all supplied lines.

12.why: Allocation: no deployer or deployer self-dealing judgment.
